acceptance.assertion: Periodic worktree hygiene is integrated into an existing runtime-retention or convergence producer; no duplicate cleanup daemon or second lifecycle truth model is introduced.

Automatic reconciliation is bounded per run and archives only clean terminal checkouts proven by exact merged PR head and default-branch evidence, while dirty, ambiguous, coordinated and foreign-owned worktrees remain fail-closed.
Automatic cleanup never bypasses active retention, recovery refs, the 24-hour archive grace, or the persisted dry-run plan and plan_sha256 precondition.

Before a new mutating worktree, broad repository lease or implementation lane is opened, one bounded read-only admission preflight checks the exact repository and requested scope for unresolved lifecycle drift, foreign dirty state, live overlapping work and sufficiently similar active task or pull-request bindings; unclear overlap blocks before state creation.

When terminal, orphaned or identity-drifted state exists in the requested scope, the operator receives a convergence-first decision and bounded next action before creating another lane. The projection alone never authorizes cleanup, lease release, process termination or task closure.

Proven disjoint parallel work remains allowed through exact path, component, process, deployment and shared-gate evidence; the implementation does not impose a global one-lane policy and does not weaken existing non-conflict, lease or merge gates.
T082 is completed successfully before periodic mutating effects are enabled.

Tests cover periodic idempotence, admission decisions, exact disjointness, stale and foreign state, gate preservation and safety boundaries; live readback demonstrates fewer avoidable new states and bounded convergence without deleting protected or active worktrees.

approval.note: User explicitly ordered prioritized implementation on 2026-07-30. Integrate scheduling and admission into existing retention, current-work and resource-coordination paths; do not introduce an independent cleanup daemon, a second lifecycle truth or a broad policy bypass.

goal: Reduce the dominant operator friction by integrating bounded worktree lifecycle reconciliation and a convergence-first WIP admission preflight into existing Grabowski retention, current-work and resource-coordination paths. New mutating lanes remain fail-closed on unresolved or overlapping state, while exact disjoint parallel work stays available and all existing recovery, retention, review, CI and merge gates remain intact.

metadata.live_basis: The deployed hygiene grip exists, but current evidence on 2026-07-30 showed 219 projected Grabowski work states with 160 blocking and 101 worktrees, while the wider five-repository projection showed 324 states with 258 blocking and 520 worktrees. Seven-day audit evidence showed 616 Bureau failure statuses, 654 effects not started and 34 repeated repo.worktree.ensure blockades. The task therefore combines downstream reconciliation with upstream admission control.
